name: Agrippa
overview: Agrippa, also known as Herod Agrippa II, was a male king noted in the New Testament as the ruler who visited Festus. His unique attribute identifies him specifically in Acts 25:13, where he appears as a significant political figure. Scripture does not provide information about his tribe.
namesAndTitles: Agrippa is primarily known by the proper name 'Agrippa,' with no specific meaning given in the biblical text. He is also referred to by the title 'King Agrippa,' indicating his royal status as a monarch, as noted in Acts 25:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Agrippa beyond what is indicated by his title as king. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Agrippa's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role as the king who interacted with the Roman governor Festus, situating him within the political context of the early church. His presence in Acts 25:13 highlights the intersection of Roman authority and Jewish leadership during the time of the apostles. As Herod Agrippa II, he represents the continuation of Herodian rule during a critical period of Christian witness and legal proceedings.
